title: Hedera’s $0.102 support: The line that can spark a 31% rally
summary: The potential support level on the chart remains critical to HBAR’s next move, but only if traders defend this level.
content: Hedera's HBAR token is currently testing a critical price support level at $0.102. Market analysts indicate that this specific chart level could serve as the foundation for a potential 31% price rally. However, this bullish scenario depends entirely on traders successfully defending the $0.102 support line to prevent further downward movement.
content_ta: Hedera-வின் HBAR டோக்கன் தற்போது $0.102 என்ற முக்கியமான விலை ஆதரவு நிலையில் வர்த்தகமாகி வருகிறது. இந்த குறிப்பிட்ட நிலை தக்கவைக்கப்பட்டால் 31% வரை விலை உயர வாய்ப்புள்ளது என்று சந்தை ஆய்வாளர்கள் தெரிவிக்கின்றனர். எனினும், வர்த்தகர்கள் இந்த $0.102 ஆதரவு கோட்டைப் பாதுகாத்தால் மட்டுமே இந்த விலை உயர்வு சாத்தியமாகும்.

title: Citi launches multi-market instant payments on Swift scheme
summary: Citi has gone live with multiple markets on the Swift payments scheme, enabling bank clients to access multiple cross-border instant payment markets through a single account structure.
content: Citi has successfully launched multi-market instant payments utilizing the Swift scheme. This rollout allows institutional bank clients to seamlessly access multiple cross-border instant payment markets through a single, consolidated account structure, streamlining international transactions and enhancing efficiency for corporate users operating across different regions.
content_ta: Citi நிறுவனம் Swift திட்டத்தின் மூலம் பல சந்தைகளில் உடனடி பணப் பரிவர்த்தனை சேவையைத் தொடங்கியுள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் வங்கியின் வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் ஒரே கணக்கின் மூலமாக பல்வேறு நாடுகளின் எல்லை கடந்த உடனடிப் பணப் பரிவர்த்தனை சந்தைகளை எளிதாக அணுக முடியும்.

title: Zilch eyes 2027 London IPO
summary: Zilch is in talks with banks as it prepares to go public, with the UK-based buy now, pay later provider reportedly leaning towards a London listing.
content: UK-based buy now, pay later provider Zilch is reportedly preparing for an initial public offering in London as early as 2027. The company has begun holding discussions with banks to lay the groundwork for going public, with a London listing currently appearing as the favored option for the financial firm's market debut.

title: MetaMask exits Ethereum validators amid undisclosed security incident
summary: MetaMask said it is investigating the threat internally and said it has found no immediate threat to its wallets.
content: Popular cryptocurrency platform MetaMask has withdrawn from operating Ethereum validators following an undisclosed security incident. The company announced it is currently investigating the situation internally. Officials confirmed that despite the incident involving its validator operations, no immediate threats have been detected regarding user wallets, ensuring that funds remain secure while the investigation continues.
content_ta: பிரபலமான கிரிப்டோகரன்சி தளமான MetaMask, வெளியிடப்படாத பாதுகாப்பு சம்பவம் ஒன்றைத் தொடர்ந்து Ethereum வேலிடேட்டர்களை இயக்குவதில் இருந்து விலகியுள்ளது. இந்தச் சூழ்நிலையை தாங்கள் உள்நாட்டில் விசாரித்து வருவதாக நிறுவனம் அறிவித்துள்ளது. வேலிடேட்டர் செயல்பாடுகளை இந்தச் சம்பவம் பாதித்திருந்தாலும், பயனர்களின் வாலெட்டுகளுக்கு உடனடி அச்சுறுத்தல் எதுவும் கண்டறியப்படவில்லை என்று அதிகாரிகள் உறுதிப்படுத்தினர், இதன் மூலம் விசாரணை தொடரும் வரை நிதிகள் பாதுகாப்பாக இருக்கும்.

title: New Bitcoin upgrade catches hidden key leaks hiding the exact fix
summary:
BIP461 would make compliant ECDSA signatures reproducible, enabling comparisons that flag deviations without proving malicious firmware.
The post New Bitcoin upgrade catches hidden key leaks hiding the exact fix appeared first on CryptoSlate.
content: A proposed Bitcoin upgrade known as BIP461 aims to detect hidden key leaks by making ECDSA signatures reproducible. This update allows for easy comparisons that can flag deviations in firmware without requiring proof of malicious intent. The enhancement provides a new layer of security and transparency for users navigating potential vulnerabilities in the network.

content_ta: Wells Fargo நிறுவனத்தின் ஆய்வாளர் Mike Mayo, வங்கிப் பங்குகளில் செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு (AI) ஏற்படுத்தும் பாதிப்புகள் குறித்த முதலீட்டாளர்களின் அச்சம் தேவையற்றது என்று கூறியுள்ளார். வங்கித் துறையில் வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கு இருக்கும் நம்பிக்கையே, AI-யால் எளிதில் தகர்க்க முடியாத ஒரு மிகப்பெரிய பலம் என்று அவர் குறிப்பிடுகிறார். சந்தை தற்போது எச்சரிக்கையுடன் செயல்பட்டாலும், நீண்டகால அடிப்படையில் வங்கியின் ஸ்திரத்தன்மையும், வாடிக்கையாளர் உறவுகளும் அந்தத் துறையின் வலுவான அடித்தளமாகத் திகழ்கின்றன.

Such a move could hold significant implications for international crypto markets, as global regulators observe how major economies navigate the integration of digital assets within their existing financial systems.
content_ta: Solana Co. நிர்வாகத்தின் கருத்துப்படி, சீனா தனது நாட்டின் கிரிப்டோகரன்சி துறையை நிர்வகிக்க தனித்துவமான அணுகுமுறையை உருவாக்கும் என்று எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது. தொழில்நுட்ப கண்டுபிடிப்புகளையும் அரசின் கட்டுப்பாட்டையும் சமநிலைப்படுத்தும் வகையில் சீனாவின் இந்த ஒழுங்குமுறை மாற்றங்கள் அமையலாம். உலகின் மிகப்பெரிய பொருளாதாரங்களில் ஒன்றான சீனா டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்களை எவ்வாறு கையாள்கிறது என்பது, உலகளாவிய கிரிப்டோ சந்தைகளிலும் மற்ற நாடுகளின் ஒழுங்குமுறை கொள்கைகளிலும் குறிப்பிடத்தக்க தாக்கத்தை ஏற்படுத்தக்கூடும்.

content_ta: Tencent நிறுவனம் Oracle-இடம் இருந்து 1,00,000 AI சிப்களை ஐந்து ஆண்டுகளுக்கு குத்தகைக்கு எடுக்கும் முக்கிய ஒப்பந்தத்தை செய்துள்ளது. செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு உள்கட்டமைப்பை வலுப்படுத்தவும், தொழில்நுட்ப சந்தையில் போட்டித்தன்மையை தக்கவைக்கவும் இந்த நடவடிக்கை உதவும். title: Backbase Appoints Roland Booijen as Chief Product Officer, Agentic Banking
summary:
Backbase, the company behind the AI-native Banking OS, announced today that it has appointed Roland Booijen to Chief Product Officer, Agentic Banking. Booijen will lead the Agentic Banking product strategy across Conversational Banking, Relationship Intelligence, and Customer Operations.
The appointment comes five months after Backbase launched its AI-native Banking OS and follows the recent acquisition of Kasisto, a pioneer in conversational and agentic AI for banking. 
Backbase’s AI-Native Banking OS is the operating system that banks use to run their frontline operations where employees and AI agents work together across the customer lifecycle, from front-office to back-office. In the new role, Booijen will set the roadmap for those agents, which take action and resolve everyday banking requests end to end, freeing relationship managers to focus on clients. He continues to report to Jouk Pleiter, Backbase's founder and CEO, as key player of the executive team steering the company's shift from digital banking software to an AI-native operating system that banks use to unify their frontline.
Booijen has spent more than a decade in banking technology product leadership, most recently as Backbase’s General Manager for Ecosystems, where he led Backbase’s Marketplace and Connector product, technology & commercial strategy. Booijen is also the Founder of the widely popular Dutch Payment App, Tikkie, and has held various director roles at ABN AMRO before joining Backbase.
This appointment lands as banks move AI from isolated pilots toward enterprise investment and executive-level priorities. Salesforce reports that the adoption of AI agents in customer service organizations increased 1.7x from 2025 to 2026 and that 70% of customer service organizations that adopt AI agents observe measurable value within 60 days of deployment.
"Roland has spent years building the products that took us from digital banking to agentic banking. Giving him this mandate now, reflects our dedication to lead the charge in this space. He's the right person to take our agents to the frontline to serve millions of people around the world", commented Jouk Pleiter, Founder and CEO at Backbase.

title: Brits Trust AI More with Their Health than with Their Money
summary:
UK consumers trust artificial intelligence more with their health and their legal problems than they do with their money, according to new research from Enfuce, Europe's card issuing and processing powerhouse. The findings point to a payments-specific trust gap. And as AI moves deeper behind every transaction, it's arriving in the one place people already struggle to see, understand and trust.
Key findings:
37% of UK adults would trust AI to help with a health symptom and 38% with a legal question, and just 22% for making or managing a payment
Of ten everyday tasks tested, payments ranked last for AI trust, behind general search (63%), navigation (57%) and recommendations (56%), and last for actual use: among AI users, 53% have used it for general search and 26% for health symptoms, versus 10% for savings and investments and 8% for payments
Consumers also find payments hard to understand: 48% think only one or two companies are involved in processing a card payment, and just 27% feel they understand well how their payments are kept secure
45% would feel uncomfortable making a payment if they knew fraud detection was handled by AI rather than a human team; only 23% would feel comfortable
Payments already have an accountability blind spot
The reluctance to trust AI with money reflects a payments system that is not well understood and, as a result, not fully trusted. Almost half (48%) think only one or two companies are involved in processing a card payment, when a typical transaction can involve five or more, and just 27% feel they understand well how their payments are kept secure.
Without visibility into the system, confidence rests on who people recognise: 88% trust banks and card networks to keep their money secure, compared to just 41% for fintech and payment apps. The same logic shapes which methods feel safe, the ones consumers know and understand rate highest. Cash and direct debit both score 82%, while newer, less visible ways to pay inspire less confidence: contactless at 64% and digital wallets at 57%.
The system also has an accountability problem when things go wrong. No single party is named as mainly responsible for the loss by more than a quarter of consumers, 23% point to the platform where the scam originated, 21% to the consumer, 15% to the consumer's bank, and 15% simply don't know.
Asked what would most increase their trust in a payment method, 30% said knowing they would get their money back if something goes wrong, more than the next three factors combined: strong fraud protection (19%), personal data protection (8%) and provider reputation (6%).
Even as a safeguard, AI isn't trusted
Consumers are reluctant to involve AI in payments even when its role is purely protective. 95% would accept at least one additional safeguard in exchange for more secure payments, including approval being required before a payment (47%), additional identity checks (43%), reimbursement protection and access to human support (36%). Yet just 19% would accept AI-led fraud detection as that safeguard and 45% would feel uncomfortable making a payment knowing fraud detection was handled by AI rather than a human team, against only 23% who would feel comfortable.
Nine in ten (90%) have at least one concern about AI being used to detect payment fraud, led by fear of AI making mistakes (51%), data privacy (39%) and cybersecurity risk (35%). Even in a protective role, AI has yet to earn the trust consumers place in human oversight.
Taken together, the findings point to a payments system where trust rests on what consumers can see and understand, and where AI, for now, sits outside that. 
“We spent decades making payments invisible, tap, pay, move on. Yet our research shows people are more willing to trust AI with a legal question than with a payment. Our industry needs to take that hesitation seriously. Customers should be able to trust that their money is protected, that someone is accountable for it, and that there is somewhere to turn when something goes wrong. Payments can stay invisible. Trust cannot.” Denise Johansson, CEO and Co-founder, Enfuce.

title: iplicit Opens Newcastle Office as It Extends Its Leading Position in the UK Mid-Market

The firm was named today by Statista and the Financial Times as one of the UK's Fastest Growing Companies 2027, its third consecutive year being recognised for growth by the two organisations, following its placements on the FT 1000 list in 2024 and 2025.
iplicit operates a remote-first model and has grown its team to over 230 people, with around 90% of its people distributed across the UK and almost 80% based outside London and the Southeast.
With an existing office in Bournemouth, the firm has seen its southern team benefit from the option to work on a hybrid basis and will now extend the same option to its growing northern sales and commercial team.

US and international expansion will be next, and it begins once we have fully conquered this market."

title: Survey: 63% of Americans Open to Letting AI Choose Brands for 20% Savings
summary:
A nationwide survey of 2,000 U.S. adults conducted by Talker Research on behalf of Spreedly found that 63% would or might allow an AI shopping assistant to choose brands for them if it consistently saved them 20% on purchases.
The findings come as AI shopping agents such as Meta’s new Muse move from product discovery into checkout, raising new questions about how much purchasing control consumers are willing to hand to AI. The survey suggests the relationship between consumers and brands could change significantly as AI becomes more involved in purchasing decisions.
Brand loyalty appears especially vulnerable among younger consumers. Thirty-four percent of Gen Z and 30% of Millennials said they would give up brand loyalty if an AI assistant consistently found the best products at the lowest prices. Among parents with children under five, 60% said they would allow AI to choose brands if doing so consistently saved them 20%.
The shift is also visible in product research. Across all respondents, Google Search remains the most trusted source at 25%, followed by friends and family at 22%. Among Gen Z, however, 31% selected ChatGPT as the source they trust most for product research, compared with 12% for Google Search. ChatGPT also ranked ahead of friends and family, online reviews, and retailer websites among Gen Z respondents.
“Consumers may increasingly rely on an agent to decide which brand wins the purchase, but they still expect control when money moves,” said Justin Benson, CEO of Spreedly. “That changes the transaction environment for merchants.”
Consumers will delegate choice before control
Even when AI saves consumers money, 43% say they would still insist on deciding how much to spend and 41% would retain control over which payment method is used.
Only 20% would allow an AI shopping assistant to spend money without approval, while another 16% would permit autonomous spending only for small purchases. Nearly two-thirds (64%) would not allow AI to spend without approval.
Consumers are also hesitant to give agents direct access to payment information. Only 19% would allow an AI shopping assistant access in exchange for a guarantee of the lowest price available online, while 23% said maybe and 58% said no.
Fraud remains the biggest barrier to autonomous shopping
More than half of respondents (52%) cited fear of fraud as something that would prevent them from allowing AI to complete a purchase, followed by lack of trust in AI companies (45%) and fear of overspending (40%).
Consumers also place responsibility primarily on AI providers. If an AI assistant selected a product and something went wrong, 41% said they would primarily hold the AI company responsible, compared with 13% who would blame the retailer and 6% the payment provider. 
No company has established a dominant position in consumer trust. Google ranked first among potential AI shopping providers at just 13%, followed by PayPal at 11%, Amazon at 10%, and Walmart at 10%.

title: Volt Receives Australian Financial Services Licence from ASIC, Completing Direct Regulatory Authorisation Across Australia, the UK and EU
summary:
Volt, the real-time, rail-agnostic money movement platform, today announces that its Australian entity, Volt Connect Pty Ltd, has been granted Australian Financial Services Licence (AFSL) number 700107 by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC). The licence authorises Volt to provide its account-to-account payment services – covering pay-ins and pay-outs on the New Payments Platform – to both retail and wholesale clients in Australia.
The grant completes Volt’s framework of direct regulatory authorisation across its three core markets. Volt now holds licences in its own name across the United Kingdom (Electronic Money Institution), the European Economic Area (Polish National Payment Institution) and Australia (AFSL 700107) – creating a single, unified account-to-account platform for the global merchants and PSPs Volt serves.
In Australia, Volt’s platform spans the full real-time payments lifecycle on the New Payments Platform (NPP): PayTo collections (one-off, one-click and recurring), PayID aliasing for automated reconciliation, instant pay-outs to BSB/account or PayID, and Confirmation of Payee – all accessed through the same API merchants use for Volt’s UK and EU markets. Australian merchants and partners include Primer, Optty, Pepperstone, BetMakers and City Beach.
“The Australian real-time payments infrastructure is a showcase of how A2A can reach feature parity with cards and can unlock convenience as well as better cost structures for merchants and consumers. The AFSL gives us the ability to provide our global merchants and PSPs a unified A2A experience with pay-ins and pay-outs in Europe, the UK and Australia.”– Steffen Vollert, CEO and co-founder, Volt.
“PayTo and PayID gave Australian merchants a real-time alternative to card rails for collections. The AFSL extends that to payouts – instant refunds, claims disbursements, marketplace payments and gig-economy payouts on the same NPP infrastructure. For the merchants we work with, that’s a meaningful product expansion. It’s also a clear signal of intent: Australia is a strategic market we’re investing in for the long term, not a satellite operation.”– Kristofer Rogers, SVP Australia and New Zealand, Volt.
With AFSL 700107 in place, Volt operates its account-to-account platform under its own regulatory authority across three of the world’s most advanced real-time payments markets: the United Kingdom, the European Economic Area and Australia.

title: Introducing Cribl Detect, Delivering a New Way to SIEM
summary:
Cribl, the AI Platform for Telemetry, today announced Cribl Detect, built on the company’s open data platform to provide a complete SIEM at up to 50% less cost than other companies. Cribl Detect gives security teams a better way to detect, investigate, and respond to threats without locking their telemetry into another monolithic, single-vendor stack. Cribl’s new platform-first approach lets customers adapt and customise their SIEM to their unique security operations. This announcement brings Cribl into the $8.2 billion SIEM market.
AI-generated attacks increase both the speed and sophistication of threats, putting pressure on security teams to detect and respond faster. Since Cribl Detect runs on the company’s agentic AI-powered platform, with built-in inference and an agentic runtime, it can move beyond static, rules-based detection. Intelligence from Cribl’s AI security operations center (AI SOC) capabilities helps automate detection and investigation workflows, applying analytics closer to the data to surface high-fidelity, actionable signals, reduce noise, and prioritise the threats that matter most. Together, these capabilities help security teams find blind spots and improve security outcomes.
Security teams face difficult choices with today’s SIEMs
For years, security teams frustrated with their SIEMs have faced two flawed options. Legacy monolithic SIEMs offer integration without choice, forcing customers into one vendor’s schema, one vendor’s pricing model, and per-gigabyte economics that turn analysis into a tax. Newer “SIEM-less” stacks assembled on general-purpose data platforms offer choice without integration. Teams get to pick their tools, but they also become the integrator, stitching together separate schemas, contracts, and pipelines themselves. Cribl Detect is designed to offer the best parts of both: the openness and customisability of a platform-first approach with the comprehensive out-of-the-box detection, investigation, and response capabilities of a purpose-built solution. This same platform approach powers Cribl’s expanding portfolio of solutions.
“Customers don’t want the SIEM they have today, and they don’t have the resources to build the SIEM they want,” said Clint Sharp, co-founder and CEO of Cribl. “With Cribl Detect, we’ve taken a different approach that solves both problems – an out-of-the-box SIEM experience built on a highly flexible platform specifically for telemetry that allows customers to adapt, mold, and even rebuild the SIEM for their specific needs. And because the platform natively integrates inference and an agentic runtime, Cribl Detect goes beyond rigid rules to catch fast-moving AI threats." 
Skip the “DIY” headaches
While a “do it yourself” approach to SIEM and security operations can sound appealing, enterprises are rarely prepared to build and support what they need. Cribl’s new way to SIEM offers an alternative that starts with the same telemetry organisations already access using the Cribl platform they already trust, in open formats they can control. This means Cribl Detect’s alerts, investigations, and analytics can run against data wherever it resides, rather than being confined or duplicated to a monolithic, single-vendor stack. With Cribl Detect, federation allows analysts to investigate across distributed telemetry in pipelines, data lakes, object stores, and existing tools. Cribl also applies detections in-stream as telemetry moves through the pipeline, bringing security logic to the data wherever it flows, getting the right signals moving earlier, so correlation and investigation can happen faster. 
A key differentiator of Cribl Detect is that its detections and detection posture management (DPM), triage with AI security operations center (AI SOC), security orchestration/automation/response (SOAR), and compliance/governance capabilities all inherit access to any data available in the platform. This makes it possible to run the product without having to move historical data first.
"Cribl Detect brings together two capabilities that matter to practitioners: investigating across data they already control and identifying detection gaps, broken rules, and missing telemetry,”  said Francis Odum, cybersecurity researcher at Software Analyst Cyber Research. “Building these capabilities into its existing data platform is a compelling direction for Cribl, giving security teams a path to modernise their SOC without creating another proprietary data silo.”
Built-In DPM and AI triage to accelerate incident response
Cribl Detect includes detection posture management that gives security teams a continuously updated view of what they are and aren’t detecting. Cribl Detect not only maps existing detections against MITRE ATT&CK techniques, surfacing coverage gaps, broken or noisy rules, and missing telemetry, but also provides recommendations and workflows for fast remediation. Alongside rules-based detections, AI SOC intelligence powers automated detection techniques that catch threats rules alone would miss. AI-driven triage, investigation, and disposition technology then helps analysts move from alert to answer faster, without manually correlating data across tools.

title: payabl. and London Lions Extend Partnership to Modernise the Club’s Payment Operations for the 2026/27 Season
summary:

As the club’s Official Payments Partner, payabl. will support London Lions’ financial operations with multi-currency business accounts and corporate cards, helping the club manage payments, spending and international activity as it continues to grow.
The expanded partnership comes as London Lions enter another increasingly international season. Alongside competing domestically in Super League Basketball and across Europe in the BKT EuroCup, the club will face the Portland Trail Blazers in an NBA pre-season fixture on October 12.
Operating across markets adds complexity behind the scenes, from paying suppliers and partners in different countries to managing travel, team expenditure, and multiple currencies amid a demanding fixture schedule.
payabl.’s business accounts enable London Lions to hold and manage multiple currencies, make domestic and cross-border payments and monitor their finances from one place. Combined with payabl.’s corporate cards, the club can manage day-to-day business expenditure with greater control and visibility.
Both solutions are accessible through payabl.one, bringing more of the club’s financial activity into a single platform and reducing the need to manage multiple providers across disconnected systems.
Steve Devereux, CEO of London Lions, said: “As London Lions grows, the operation behind the club has to grow with it. We are competing across the UK and Europe, travelling internationally and working with more partners across different markets, so managing money efficiently becomes increasingly important.
“Having our accounts and spending in one place gives us much better visibility and control over the day-to-day operation. It means our team can spend less time managing financial admin and more time focused on growing the club.”
Kristaps Zips, UK CEO at payabl., said: “When an organisation starts operating across more markets, financial complexity grows quickly: more currencies, more payments, more suppliers and more day-to-day expenditure. By bringing business accounts and corporate cards together through payabl.one, we can give the Lions greater visibility and control over how money moves across the organisation as they continue to grow.”
As part of the renewed sponsorship agreement, payabl. branding continues to feature across London Lions home games during the 2026/27 season. It features on the jerseys and warm-up kits of both the men’s and women’s teams, alongside in-arena LED and scoreboard advertising and digital and social media activations.
The partnership reflects payabl.’s continued investment in the UK market and its focus on supporting internationally ambitious organisations as they grow across markets.

title: inDrive.Money Expands Access to Financial Services as Driver Loans More Than Double in Latin America
summary:
inDrive, a global mobility and delivery platform operating across 47 countries, today announced that the number of loans taken out by drivers through inDrive.Money more than doubled in the first half of 2026 across Latin America, rising 118% year-on-year, as more drivers turned to the platform for fair, transparent access to cash loans.
Growth was strong across every market, with demand in Peru, Colombia and Mexico rising by 128%, 88% and 71%, respectively. Brazil, which launched inDrive.Money in August 2025, saw growth of more than 400% as the offering gained momentum in its first year of being offered in Latin America’s largest country.
Gig economy workers are often excluded from accessing formal credit, due to their variable working hours and income, as well as absence of credit histories. inDrive.Money leverages alternative data on drivers’ earning patterns to help partner financial institutions make more informed and accurate credit-scoring decisions.
inDrive.Money helps unlock formal lending for drivers, making credit accessible directly via the inDrive app. Applications are simple, clear and take just a few minutes, with the approved amount, monthly repayment and loan term shown upfront. The loan size and repayments are based on each driver's earnings, with repayments taken automatically as a share of each fare. No paperwork, branch visits or manual transfers are required.
Alexander Kurchin, General Manager at inDrive.Money, commented: “The growth of inDrive.Money across Latin America shows there is a clear and expanding demand for fairer, more transparent access to loans among gig economy drivers. Many drivers have the income to repay a loan, but are overlooked by traditional lenders because their earnings do not fit conventional credit models. By using the alternative data we have access to, we can help our financial partners better understand drivers’ real earning capacity and extend financial services to people who might otherwise be excluded. Ultimately, this is about giving drivers greater financial resilience and freedom of choice, so that an unexpected expense does not stand in their way of earning a living.”
Drivers in Latin America have been shown to return to inDrive.Money for additional loans. In Mexico, an Impact Report developed with the MX Internet Association (AIMX), and published in February 2026, found that more than 11% of active drivers have accessed a personal loan through inDrive.Money, with nearly half of those drivers going on to take out more than one loan. This repeat use highlights the important role the product is playing in helping drivers manage their finances and meet their ongoing needs.
inDrive.Money is part of inDrive’s broader mission to challenge injustice by giving people greater freedom of choice in ride-hailing and beyond. The company’s core ride-hailing offering uses a peer-to-peer pricing model that allows drivers and riders to negotiate a price they both consider fair, while inDrive’s commission rates average around 10% across its markets. Both inDrive’s core ride-hailing platform and the inDrive.Money offering give drivers greater control over how they earn and how they manage their finances. inDrive’s other interconnected services, including couriers, delivery and advertising, were launched with the same mission of enabling fairer choices and more freedom of choice.
Independent research from Oxford Economics highlights the role that freedom of choice over trips and their pricing can play in supporting drivers’ financial resilience. Published in January 2026, the study found that 66% of drivers surveyed in Latin America said fare negotiation helps them earn a fair income, while nearly 64% of drivers and riders in the region said it helps them complete more trips. These findings reinforce the importance of giving drivers more control of their personal finances, both in terms of earnings and in terms of access to credit.

AVA Foundation அதன் டோக்கனாமிக்ஸ் மாற்றத்தின் ஒரு பகுதியாக புதிய லாக் லெவல்களை அறிவித்துள்ளது. ஏற்கனவே AVA-வின் புழக்கத்தில் உள்ள தொகையில் சுமார் 16% லாக் செய்யப்பட்டுள்ளது, மேலும் 30% தொகையை லாக் செய்யும் நீண்ட கால இலக்கைக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: A SWIFT-Ripple Alliance? Why A Single Rumor Just Sent The XRP Community Into A Frenzy
summary: Speculation of a potential alliance between Ripple and SWIFT, the global interbank messaging network, has exploded across social media.
content: Speculation regarding a potential partnership between Ripple and the global interbank messaging network SWIFT recently sparked excitement across social media platforms. Rumors of this alliance quickly energized the XRP community, driving significant online discussion. While no official confirmation has been provided by either organization, the unverified reports highlight the ongoing interest in how traditional financial systems and cryptocurrency networks might intersect in the future.

title: Mona Raises $3.5M to Expand Its AI Platform for Small Business Capital Access and Financial Coaching
summary:
Mona today announced an oversubscribed $3.5M round to expand its AI platform for small business capital access and financial coaching. The round was led by Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners, with participation from Alumni Ventures, Wisdom Ventures, angels including former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, and others. Mona is also backed by the Mastercard Strive USA Innovation Fund.
Small business owners navigate a fragmented ecosystem of lenders, government programs, grants, and other capital sources – without the financial teams or advisors available to larger companies. Mona brings that fragmented market into one place through its AI platform. Entrepreneurs complete a common application, which Mona uses to surface relevant opportunities, streamline applications, and tailor guidance.
Mona – recently named to Fast Company’s World Changing Ideas List – pairs AI with human coaching, offering ongoing support beyond a one-time funding search. Entrepreneurs turn to Mona as questions and opportunities arise, while the platform improves as it learns about their businesses. Mona has already supported thousands of small businesses and helped entrepreneurs secure millions in affordable capital, with early traction in Chicago, Detroit, Jacksonville, New York City, and San Francisco.
“Small businesses are the engine of the American economy, but there’s a huge market gap in the tools, guidance, and resources available to them,” said Gareth Schweitzer, Partner at Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners. “Mona is closing that gap by leveraging AI to help small business owners find capital opportunities, apply for financing, and access high-quality coaching.”
Mona was founded by Andrew Leon Hanna and Anny Dow, who met at Stanford and whose families’ stories as immigrant small business owners inspired the company’s mission.
“Small businesses create the majority of net new jobs and are the heartbeats of our communities. Yet they are expected to make high-stakes financial decisions with limited support,” said Hanna. “By pairing AI with human expertise, we’re building toward a world where every entrepreneur can have a trusted financial coach in their corner to help them grow.”
Mona is also partnering with Mastercard Strive USA, with support from the Mastercard Strive USA Innovation Fund. Through the partnership, Mona will collaborate with small business support organizations to expand its reach.
“As AI continues to disrupt industries, there is a huge opportunity to make sure small businesses are not left behind and receive the support they need to grow,” said Jonathan Fantini-Porter, Senior Vice President of Americas at the Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth.
“By combining new technology with the reach and trust of community organizations, Mona is helping improve small business financial health by increasing their cash flow, reducing financial volatility, and expanding access to affordable capital so small business owners can focus on keeping their small business dreams going.”

title: Stripe Agrees to Acquire Parafin to Expand Revenue Opportunities for Platforms and Help Small Businesses Grow
summary:
Stripe, the programmable financial services company, today announced that it has agreed to acquire Parafin, a leading embedded financial products platform. Parafin supports some of the largest and most complex platforms in the world, including DoorDash, Gusto, Jobber, and Mindbody, by providing credit offerings for their small business customers. With Parafin, Stripe will strengthen its support for ambitious platforms while bringing more credit to the small businesses driving economic growth.
More than 18,000 platforms build on Stripe, and they increasingly serve as the financial home for small businesses. Products such as Stripe Capital help these platforms generate new revenue opportunities. Recently, demand for Capital has increased as new business creation accelerates and traditional financing remains constrained. In Q2 2026, new businesses launching on Stripe increased 86% year-over-year. Meanwhile, only 41% of small business loan applications were approved in the US last year, down 18% from 2015. Access to capital matters: a recent study found that businesses that accepted Stripe Capital offers grew 27 percentage points faster than those that did not.
Since 2020, Parafin has helped more than 60,000 businesses gain access to capital and invest in growth. Alongside its core capital offering, Parafin's complementary credit products, Pay Over Time and Spend, give businesses more flexibility in how they manage cash flow.
“Platforms power millions of small businesses throughout the world and are central to Stripe’s mission,” said Neetika Bansal, business lead at Stripe. “Sahill, Vineet, and the Parafin team bring acute expertise and leadership in credit, risk, and embedded financial products. Together, we’ll be able to offer a wider range of credit products to a larger ecosystem and increase credit access for high-growth businesses.”
“We started Parafin to give small businesses access to the modern credit products that were only available to large companies,” said Sahill Poddar, cofounder and CEO of Parafin. “Stripe’s financial infrastructure and global reach will help us move faster and serve millions more businesses through the platforms they rely on.”

title: Chubb Life Hong Kong Unveils New Multi-Currency Insurance Plan
summary:
Chubb Life Hong Kong today announced the launch of the Chubb MyLegacy Multi-Currency Insurance Plan (“Chubb MyLegacy Multi-Currency” or the “Plan”), expanding its flagship Chubb MyLegacy series. Designed for families seeking greater flexibility in their legacy planning, the Plan introduces a first-in-market 1 customized life event settlement option and offers policyholders the ability to convert the policy to another available currency.
As high-net-worth and affluent families in Hong Kong navigate shifting global market dynamics, demand has evolved beyond basic currency conversion towards tailored legacy planning. Customers often require flexible withdrawal options without sacrificing long-term capital growth potential. Chubb MyLegacy Multi-Currency addresses these needs through its distinctive features:
Legacy Planning Adaptability: First-in-market1 customized life event settlement option allows customers to pre-set financial payouts triggered by key life milestones—such as university graduation, marriage, or home purchase, passing on assets on their own exact terms without the threshold and setup complexity of typical trusts.
Multi-Currency Governance: Customers may use the Currency Conversion Option2 starting from the 3rd Policy Anniversary to convert the policy to another available policy currency of choice, providing greater flexibility in cross-border wealth management.
Flexible Withdrawal Options: Pre-set withdrawal instructions also offer a financial safety net for life’s uncertainties. Customers may also use a one-time or regular cash withdrawals, or select an annuity option, while preserving underlying funds for long-term legacy planning.
Multi-Generational Succession: To ensure seamless continuity across generations, policyowners can appoint up to 5 Interim Owners, Successor Owners, and Successor Insureds each.
Alex Wong, Chief Customer Proposition Officer of Chubb Life Hong Kong, said, “Chubb MyLegacy Multi-Currency Insurance Plan is built for what matters most to our customers—flexibility, security, and the ability to grow and protect their wealth across generations. By combining tailored legacy planning features with currency flexibility and practical withdrawal options, we are helping families protect and grow their wealth in a way that better reflects their needs today and their aspirations for tomorrow.”

title: Apple Pay Launches in India
summary:
Starting today, Apple Pay is available for users in India across iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch, with support for Mac coming soon.1 The launch brings Apple customers an easy, secure, and private way to pay in stores, in apps, and on the web at retailers of all sizes — all without the need to type in PINs or use OTPs at checkout. Customers with Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards can add their cards to Apple Pay and use them at thousands of in-store and online merchants across India, as well as anywhere that accepts NFC transactions.
“India is home to a dynamic and digitally savvy population that continues to embrace a cashless future while expecting the highest standards of security and privacy, and we’re so excited to bring Apple Pay to users in India today,” said Jennifer Bailey, Apple’s vice president of Apple Pay and Apple Wallet. “Apple Pay makes everyday payments with a card easy, secure, and private — from simply tapping to pay in stores without an extra app, PIN, or OTP to checking out online without repeatedly entering payment information.”
“We are at a significant inflection point in payments, where technology, security and changing customer expectations are reshaping how people transact. At Axis Bank, our aspiration is to remain at the forefront of this transformation by building payment experiences that are progressive, trusted and deeply relevant to our customers,” said Amitabh Chaudhry, MD & CEO, Axis Bank. "The introduction of Apple Pay advances this ambition, bringing greater choice and flexibility to our Credit Card customers, with support across the Mastercard and Visa networks. As payments become increasingly embedded in customers’ everyday digital lives, our focus is on bringing together innovation and trust, while making every interaction more intuitive and relevant. More importantly, this reflects our vision of a more connected and sophisticated payments ecosystem, where technology enables convenience and confidence in every transaction.”
“As India’s digital economy accelerates and consumers seek seamless and secure payment experiences, the introduction of Apple Pay for our Axis Bank-issued Mastercard credit card holders ushers in a new era of contactless commerce, giving Indian consumers greater confidence and peace of mind with every transaction,” said Gautam Aggarwal, Mastercard’s president of India and South Asia. “With Mastercard’s tokenisation technology, every Apple Pay transaction is protected by a unique, cryptographically secured token, ensuring card details are never shared with merchants, safeguarding consumers against fraud.”
“The launch of Apple Pay in India marks an important milestone in the evolution of the country’s digital payments journey,” said Suresh Sethi, Visa’s group country manager of India and South Asia. “By bringing together Apple’s intuitive consumer experience with Visa’s trusted global network and tokenisation capabilities, Apple Pay brings consumers in India a simpler, safer, and more seamless way to pay. Together, we are expanding consumer choice and helping shape the next generation of commerce in India.”
Delivering a Secure and Private Payment Experience
Security and privacy are at the core of Apple Pay. When customers use a card with Apple Pay, the actual card numbers are not stored on the device or on Apple servers, nor are they shared by Apple with the merchant. Instead, a unique Device Account Number is assigned, encrypted, and securely stored in the Secure Element, an industry-standard certified chip designed to store the payment information safely on the device.
Apple does not retain transaction information that can be tied back to the user. Their transactions stay between the user, the merchant, and their bank or card issuer. If a user’s iPhone is lost or stolen, they can use the Find My app to quickly locate, lock, or suspend payments from that device.
How to Use Apple Pay 
Apple Pay is easy to set up. Customers can add a card directly to Apple Wallet via the latest version of the Axis Bank app. Alternatively, simply open the Wallet app on iPhone, tap the plus sign, and follow the steps to add an eligible card. Once a user adds a card to their Apple device, they can start using Apple Pay right away.
Using Apple Pay in stores is seamless and easy. Simply double-click the side button or Home button; authenticate using Face ID, Touch ID, or a device passcode if prompted; and hold the top of the iPhone or display of the Apple Watch near the contactless reader to pay.
Users can also make purchases with Apple Pay on iPhone and iPad — with support for Mac coming soon — for faster and more convenient payments in apps or on the web without having to create accounts or repeatedly type in contact information, card details, or shipping and billing information.
When using Apple Pay, users will continue to earn the rewards and benefits offered by their cards.
At launch, Apple Pay will be accepted by millions of merchants across India, including at Apple Store locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, Ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, Zomato, and more. Apple has worked closely with payment service providers (PSPs) — like BillDesk, Cashfree, Juspay, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Razorpay, and more — to bring Apple Pay to their merchant networks in India, with even more merchants and apps coming over time.
Today Apple Pay is available in more than 90 countries and regions, and works with more than 11,000 bank and network partners worldwide.

title: U.S. Bank Launches New Credit Cards for Small Business Owners with Jessica Alba as Spokesperson
summary:
U.S. Bank doubles down on its commitment to support small business owners with the launch of its U.S. Bank Business EssentialsTM Visa® Card and U.S. Bank Business EssentialsTM Plus Visa Signature® Card. The cards are designed for small business owners looking for straight-forward rewards on their everyday business purchases. Both offer unlimited 2% cash back on eligible purchases, plus the ability to earn higher cash back when paired with qualifying balances in a qualified business checking account. The card launch also debuts Jessica Alba, an experienced small business owner and actress, as the bank’s new small business spokesperson.
Business EssentialsTM and Business EssentialsTM Plus help small business owners increase their financial flexibility by offering expanded purchasing capacity to manage day-to-day expenses and improve cash flow management. Plus, by connecting their banking relationship, owners benefit from seamless cash back reward redemption into their qualifying business checking account or as a statement credit on their card. This allows owners to lower their operating costs by reinvesting back into their business.
Knowing small business owners want to spend more time growing their business than managing it, the cards allow them to centralize business expenses, protect against fraud and access spend management tools. The goal is to provide peace of mind when making business purchases and to make these purchases even more rewarding when owners manage both payments and banking with U.S. Bank.
“Small business owners employ over 61 million Americans and contribute to nearly half of our nation’s GDP; they deserve financial products that reward their ambition and empower them to succeed,” said Courtney Kelso, senior executive vice president of Payments, Consumer and Small Business. “Our new Business EssentialsTM cards offer small business owners straightforward, easy-to-use benefits that help simplify their spending, banking and expense management.”
Key features include:
“Our goal is to build long-lasting relationships with small business owners through integrated solutions, not simply give them a card,” Kelso said. “The Business EssentialsTM and Business EssentialsTM Plus cards reward the strength of small businesses that build deeper connections with U.S. Bank.”
The cards also integrate key capabilities from U.S. Bank’s broader small-business banking services. The award-winning Spend Management platform comes with both the Business EssentialsTM and Business EssentialsTM Plus cards. With Spend Management, small business owners can easily capture receipts, track card spend, set card controls and integrate with existing accounting software. Also included is U.S. Bank Extend Pay, providing a convenient fixed-fee payment plan for large purchases.
Jessica Alba Campaign Launch
The Business EssentialsTM cards launch includes a new advertising and marketing campaign featuring U.S. Bank’s new small business card spokesperson, Jessica Alba.
Alba rose to public prominence as an actress in the early 2000s, but she is equally famous for her work as an entrepreneur and philanthropist. She will appear in digital and television ads for U.S. Bank’s Business EssentialsTM and Business EssentialsTM Plus credit cards.
“Jessica is an ideal representative for our Business EssentialsTM cardholders as she embodies many of the traits we celebrate among small business owners, including a tireless work ethic and the knowledge of what it takes to grow a business,” Kelso said.

title: PayPal Survey Reveals Holiday Spending Isn't Slowing Down, but Shoppers Are Changing How They Spend
summary:
Holiday shoppers aren't necessarily spending less this year. They're changing how they spend. PayPal today released its 2026 Holiday Shopping Survey, revealing that nearly six in 10 Americans (58%) feel greater financial concern heading into the holidays, yet 64% still expect to spend the same or more than they did last holiday season. Faced with that tension, shoppers are planning earlier, setting budgets and looking for more ways to get value from every purchase.
More than half (58%) plan to shop before Thanksgiving, while 67% are more likely to shop with a retailer that offers rewards or cash back. As consumers rethink how they manage holiday spending, PayPal offers more choice and flexibility through Pay Later options, rewarding ways to pay, and offers from top brands in the new PayPal app.
"What's changing isn't consumers' desire to spend during the holidays, but how they're going about it," said Frank Keller, President of Checkout Solutions & PayPal. "Shoppers are starting earlier and taking a more intentional approach, looking for deals, rewards and cash back to make every purchase count while still prioritizing the gifts and moments that matter most. As they look for ways to stretch their budgets, PayPal helps them turn that planning into action by bringing together offers, rewards and flexible payment options, including PayPal Pay Later, throughout the holiday season."
Consumers Are Taking Action to Make Holiday Budgets Go Further
With financial concerns top of mind, shoppers are taking practical steps to manage holiday spending and find value from every purchase, including:
Prioritizing budgets: Setting and sticking to a budget (36%) is the top way consumers plan to manage their holiday spending, followed by comparing prices (32%) and waiting for sales or promotions (31%).
Starting earlier: Two in five consumers plan to begin their holiday shopping by the end of October, and 29% plan to start shopping earlier than last year.
Maximizing rewards: More than two-thirds (67%) are willing to use all their saved rewards to help purchase the perfect gift, and 55% have saved rewards they could use for holiday shopping.
In addition to discovering deals from favorite brands in the PayPal app, shoppers can use the PayPal Cashback Mastercard®1 to earn 3% cash back on eligible purchases when they check out with PayPal.
Shoppers Are Making Tradeoffs to Preserve Gift-Giving
As holiday gift-giving remains a priority, consumers are making careful choices about where to cut back as they balance the season with financial pressures and rising costs.
Sacrifices are personal first: Consumers would cut back on dining out (39%) and gifts for themselves (35%) to make room for holiday spending.
Gift lists may be a little shorter: Twenty-nine percent would buy gifts for fewer people, while 34% would spend less on each individual gift.
Trading time for the perfect gift: Seventy percent are willing to visit multiple stores, while 63% would spend hours searching online for the perfect gift.
As shoppers plan their holiday gift list, clothing (52%), toys and games (38%), and beauty, personal care and fragrance (32%) are the top categories where they plan to buy this holiday season. For larger purchases or gifts for multiple people, flexible payment options from PayPal provide shoppers with another way to manage when and how they pay while keeping meaningful gift-giving within reach.
The survey also points to strong interest in flexible payment options such as Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL), as shoppers consider how to manage the timing and cost of planned holiday expenses. PayPal helps meet that need with Pay Later options including Pay in 42, which allows shoppers to split eligible purchases into four interest-free payments, and Pay Monthly3, which offers longer-term monthly payment plans. The survey found:
BNPL is a core part of the holiday payment mix: More than half of consumers (55%) have used or considered BNPL. Among those consumers, three-quarters plan to use or are considering using BNPL for holiday shopping.
Flexibility and control drive interest: Feeling more in control of their holiday budget and spreading the cost of purchases over time are each valued as BNPL benefits by 59% of consumers, while the flexibility to choose when and how to pay and the ability to take advantage of promotions are each valued by 60%.
BNPL can influence purchase decisions: Forty-two percent say they would be more likely to make a purchase if BNPL were available, 56% value BNPL's ability to help them manage the cost of a higher-value gift, and 57% say it would help them manage the cost of gifts for several people.

title: Mastercard Advances Agentic Commerce with New Trust and Intelligence Services
summary:
Today, Mastercard announced an expansion of Agent Pay, its agentic payments program, with new trust and intelligence services that provide greater context for AI-initiated transactions. By bringing together identity, intent, behavioral and fraud insights, the services give financial institutions and merchants a clearer, shared understanding of AI-driven activity – enabling smarter authorization decisions, less unnecessary friction and more seamless experiences for consumers. 
These new services form the intelligence layer of Mastercard's Agent Pay Trust Framework, which brings together identity, intent, controls, execution and intelligence to establish trust across agentic commerce.
The next era of commerce requires more context behind every payment 
Agentic commerce is moving into the mainstream, with one in 10 consumers projected to routinely use agents to make purchases by 2030. As agentic commerce grows, banks and merchants need to understand when an agent is involved, what it has been asked to do and whether the activity is legitimate. At the same time, consumers expect every transaction to be secure, no matter how they choose to pay or which agents they use.
“AI agents will make commerce more intuitive, efficient and personal — but only if people and businesses can trust the systems acting on their behalf,” said Ann Johnson, executive vice president, Security Solutions at Mastercard. “By adding new agentic intelligence and risk insights to each transaction, we are giving people the confidence to say ‘yes,’ however they choose to pay.”
A probability score identifies AI-initiated transactions 
The first service, rolling out for testing in the U.S., is a probability score indicating the likelihood that a transaction was initiated by an AI agent – giving issuers the confidence to approve legitimate agent-led purchases. Over time, Mastercard will strengthen this score with more intelligence related to behavior, merchant risk, transaction patterns, credential risk and consumer propensity, providing an even clearer picture of AI-driven activity across the transaction lifecycle.
A shared intelligence layer provides more context around AI-led purchases 
Beyond the probability score, the new agentic trust and intelligence signals give ecosystem participants a common understanding of what is happening behind a purchase by answering the following questions: 
Is the activity consistent with expected behavior or patterns?
Does the agent, merchant, credential or transaction show anything unusual that requires further review?
Should the transaction be approved or are additional checks needed?
For example, imagine asking a new AI assistant to plan and book your next trip. It finds the best flight, hotel and transportation options, then completes the bookings with a single approval. Although multiple purchases across different merchants may appear unusual on the surface, Mastercard’s insights provide the context banks and merchants need to approve legitimate activity, helping consumers move seamlessly from planning to booking the trip. If something looks risky, the transaction can be flagged for additional review before the consumer completes the purchase.

content: On day two of Sibos 2026 in Miami, major global banks including BNY, BNP Paribas, Deutsche Bank, Citi, and HSBC showcased operational AI agents. AI இந்த தானியங்கி செயல்முறைகளைக் கையாண்டாலும், மிக முக்கியமான முடிவுகளை எடுப்பதற்கு மனிதர்களின் மேற்பார்வையும் தீர்ப்பும் அவசியமாகவே வைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளதாக நிதி நிறுவனங்கள் வலியுறுத்தின.

content_ta: வங்கிகள் தங்களுடைய வாடிக்கையாளர்களுடன் உள்ள நிதித் தொடர்புகளை ஆழப்படுத்தவும், அதிக கட்டுப்பாடு மற்றும் உரிமையைக் கொண்ட பகுதிகள் மீது கவனம் செலுத்தவும் தங்களது உத்திகளை மாற்றியமைத்து வருகின்றன. கடந்த பத்தாண்டுகளில் டிஜிட்டல் அனுபவங்கள் மற்றும் தயாரிப்பு வரம்புக்காக fintech நிறுவனங்களுடன் போட்டியிட்டதைத் தாண்டி, வங்கிகள் இப்போது வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் விசுவாசத்தை உறுதிப்படுத்தவும் தங்களது நீண்டகால நிலையை பலப்படுத்தவும் புதிய முறைகளைக் கையாளுகின்றன.

title: Bitget’s $388M hack pushes Q3 crypto security losses past $1B
summary: Crypto security losses reached $1.26 billion in Q3 across 247 incidents, with September alone accounting for roughly $769 million.
content: Crypto security losses exceeded $1 billion in the third quarter, reaching a total of $1.26 billion across 247 incidents. A significant portion of these losses was driven by the Bitget hack, which resulted in $388 million being stolen. September proved to be the most devastating month, accounting for approximately $769 million of the quarterly losses.
content_ta: மூன்றாம் காலாண்டில் கிரிப்டோ பாதுகாப்பு இழப்புகள் 1 பில்லியன் டாலரைத் தாண்டி, 247 சம்பவங்கள் மூலம் மொத்தம் 1.26 பில்லியன் டாலரை எட்டியுள்ளன. இந்த இழப்புகளில் ஒரு முக்கிய பகுதி Bitget ஹேக் மூலம் ஏற்பட்டது, இதன் காரணமாக 388 மில்லியன் டாலர் திருடப்பட்டது. செப்டம்பர் மாதம் மிக மோசமான மாதமாக இருந்தது, இது காலாண்டு இழப்புகளில் தோராயமாக 769 மில்லியன் டாலரைக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

content_ta: டெனக்சஸ் நகரில் உள்ள வங்கி ஒன்றின் முன்னாள் ஊழியர், வாடிக்கையாளர் கணக்கிலிருந்து 50,000 டாலருக்கும் அதிகமான தொகையைத் திருடியதாகக் குற்றம் சாட்டப்பட்டுள்ளார். Laredo காவல்துறையின்படி, San Bernardo Avenue-ல் உள்ள வங்கி கிளையில் பணிபுரிந்தபோது, சந்தேக நபர் முறைகேடான முறையில் தொடர்ச்சியான டெபிட் கார்டு கட்டணங்களை மேற்கொண்டுள்ளார். இந்தச் சம்பவம் தொடர்பாக 25 வயதான Irma Yessenia Martinez மீது குற்றம் சாட்டப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: $1 Menu Gaps Show Up at California McDonald’s Stores Barely a Mile Apart
summary:
McDonald's AI pricing tool is tied to dollar-plus gaps on identical menu items at nearby California locations, according to the New York Post.
The post $1 Menu Gaps Show Up at California McDonald’s Stores Barely a Mile Apart appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
content: A recent report by the New York Post reveals that McDonald's locations in California, situated barely a mile apart, show significant pricing gaps of one dollar on identical menu items. According to the findings, this variation is tied to the company's automated pricing tools used at these nearby stores.
content_ta: New York Post வெளியிட்ட ஒரு செய்தியின்படி, California-வில் உள்ள McDonald's கிளைகளில் ஒரே மாதிரியான உணவுப் பொருட்களின் விலையில் ஒரு டாலர் வரை வித்தியாசம் இருப்பது தெரியவந்துள்ளது. ஒரு மைல் தொலைவுக்குள் அமைந்துள்ள இந்த கடைகளில் உள்ள இந்த விலை வேறுபாடு, நிறுவனத்தின் தானியங்கு விலை நிர்ணயக் கருவிகளுடன் தொடர்புடையது என்று கூறப்படுகிறது.

title: European payments groups join forces to take on US giants
summary: Some of Europe's biggest payments groups - Bancomat, Bizum, Wero, Sibs-MB WAY and Vipps MobilePay - have banded together to create a cross-continent network that can take on Visa and Mastercard.
content: Major European payments groups including Bancomat, Bizum, Wero, Sibs-MB WAY, and Vipps MobilePay have formed a cross-continental network. This strategic alliance aims to compete directly against dominant US payment giants like Visa and Mastercard, strengthening Europe's domestic payment infrastructure and fostering greater financial autonomy across the region.
content_ta: Bancomat, Bizum, Wero, Sibs-MB WAY மற்றும் Vipps MobilePay உள்ளிட்ட ஐரோப்பாவின் முக்கிய பேமெண்ட் நிறுவனங்கள் இணைந்து ஒரு புதிய குறுங்கண்ட நெட்வொர்க்கை உருவாக்கியுள்ளன. Visa மற்றும் Mastercard போன்ற அமெரிக்காவின் பெரிய நிறுவனங்களுக்கு போட்டியாக திகழ இந்த கூட்டணி உருவாக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Revolut expands loyalty programme with hotel transfers
summary: Revolut, the global financial platform with over 80 million customers worldwide, has today expanded its RevPoints loyalty programme, bringing hotel transfers in-app.
content: Global financial platform Revolut has expanded its RevPoints loyalty programme by introducing hotel transfers directly within its mobile application. The feature allows the company's vast customer base to access new travel perks and manage rewards more seamlessly through the app, further enhancing the platform's growing ecosystem of financial and lifestyle services.
content_ta: உலகளாவிய நிதி தளமான Revolut தனது RevPoints லாயல்டி திட்டத்தை விரிவுபடுத்தியுள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் ஹோட்டல் டிரான்ஸ்ஃபர் வசதி நேரடியாக அதன் மொபைல் அப்ளிகேஷனில் அறிமுகப்படுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய அம்சத்தின் மூலம் பயனர்கள் தங்கள் பயண சலுகைகளை எளிதாகப் பெற்று, அப்ளிகேஷன் மூலமாகவே வெகுமதிகளை நிர்வகிக்க முடியும்.

title: The Payments Association acquires European sister organisation
summary: The Payments Association in the UK advocates for the payments and transfer sectors, including crypto participants. Today, the Payments Association says it has acquired its European counterpart, the Payments Association – EU (TPA-EU). Any monetary considerations were not revealed. Together, the two entities will now... Read More
content: The Payments Association, a prominent UK-based organization advocating for the payments and transfer sectors including crypto participants, has announced the acquisition of its European counterpart, the Payments Association – EU. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. The combined entities aim to strengthen their representation and collaboration across the payments industry in the UK and Europe.
content_ta: UK-வைச் சேர்ந்த The Payments Association நிறுவனம், crypto பங்கேற்பாளர்கள் உள்ளிட்ட பணம் செலுத்துதல் மற்றும் பரிமாற்றத் துறைகளுக்காக வாதிடுகிறது. இந்நிறுவனம் தனது ஐரோப்பிய இணை நிறுவனமான Payments Association – EU-ஐக் கைப்பற்றியுள்ளதாக அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த ஒப்பந்தத்தின் நிதி விவரங்கள் வெளியிடப்படவில்லை. இந்த இணைப்பு UK மற்றும் ஐரோப்பாவில் உள்ள பணம் செலுத்தும் துறையில் இரு நிறுவனங்களின் ஒத்துழைப்பை வலுப்படுத்தும்.

title: Gresham ships application to simplify complex reconciliation with AI
summary: Gresham, a global leader in enterprise data automation for the financial services industry, today announces the availability of Control Studio, a new AI-enabled, self-service application for its Control reconciliation product.
content: Gresham, a global leader in enterprise data automation for the financial services industry, has announced the availability of Control Studio. This new AI-enabled, self-service application is designed to simplify complex reconciliation processes for its flagship Control reconciliation product, helping financial institutions manage their data more efficiently.
content_ta: நிதி சேவைக் துறைக்கான நிறுவன தரவு ஆட்டோமேஷனில் முன்னணியில் இருக்கும் Gresham, Control Studio என்ற புதிய செயலியை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய AI அடிப்படையிலான சுய சேவை செயலி, நிறுவனங்களின் சிக்கலானிங் சரிபார்ப்பு (reconciliation) பணிகளை எளிமைப்படுத்த உதவுகிறது.

content: The Jordan FinTech Academy at the Institute of Banking Studies and the MENA Fintech Association have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to boost regional cooperation. This partnership aims to promote knowledge exchange, professional development, and stronger connections among fintech professionals and institutions in Jordan and across the MENA region, highlighting Jordan's growing importance in the financial technology ecosystem.
content_ta: Institute of Banking Studies-ன் கீழ் இயங்கும் Jordan FinTech Academy மற்றும் MENA Fintech Association ஆகியவை பிராந்திய ஒத்துழைப்பை மேம்படுத்த புரிந்துணர்வு ஒப்பந்தத்தில் கையெழுத்திட்டுள்ளன. இந்த கூட்டாண்மை அறிவு பரிமாற்றம், தொழில்முறை வளர்ச்சி மற்றும் Jordan மற்றும் MENA பிராந்தியத்தில் உள்ள fintech நிபுணர்களுக்கு இடையிலான தொடர்புகளை பலப்படுத்துவதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: StraitsX to bring first SGD-denominated stablecoin to Monad
summary: StraitsX today announced plans to bring XSGD and XUSD to the Monad network in early 2027. XSGD is planned to become the first SGD-denominated stablecoin natively issued on Monad, expanding the currencies available to developers, businesses and institutions across the network.
content: StraitsX has announced plans to integrate its XSGD and XUSD stablecoins into the Monad network by early 2027. This initiative will introduce XSGD as the first Singapore dollar-denominated stablecoin natively issued on Monad, providing developers, businesses, and institutions across the blockchain network with expanded multi-currency options for digital transactions and financial applications.
content_ta: Monad நெட்வொர்க்கில் தனது XSGD மற்றும் XUSD ஸ்டேபிள்காயின்களை 2027 ஆம் ஆண்டின் தொடக்கத்தில் கொண்டுவர உள்ளதாக StraitsX அறிவித்துள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் Monad-ல் வெளியிடப்படும் முதல் SGD-அடிப்படையிலான ஸ்டேபிள்காயினாக XSGD மாறவுள்ளது. இது டெவலப்பர்கள் மற்றும் நிறுவனங்களுக்கு டிஜிட்டல் பரிவர்த்தனைகளுக்கான புதிய பல货币 (multi-currency) வாய்ப்புகளை வழங்கும்.

title: Marex expands digital assets offering with rolling spot crypto

(“Bounce Pay”), Everlink Payment Services ULC (“FIS Everlink”), Nium Canada Corporation (“Nium”), Pesapeer Incorporated (“Pesa”), Remitly Canada, Inc. This expansion broadens representation across the payment ecosystem as the organization continues to develop and operate Canada's national payment clearing and settlement systems.

title: To PaaS or to SaaS: the answer starts with your volumes
summary: Author: A finextra community member
content: Choosing between PaaS and SaaS models for your business depends heavily on transaction and data volumes. Organizations must carefully evaluate their usage patterns and operational needs before committing to a cloud architecture. While SaaS offers out-of-the-box convenience for general applications, PaaS provides the flexibility and scalability required for handling high-volume, custom workloads effectively.
content_ta: உங்கள் நிறுவனத்திற்கு PaaS அல்லது SaaS மாதிரிகளில் எதைத் தேர்ந்தெடுப்பது என்பது பரிவர்த்தனை மற்றும் தரவு அளவுகளைப் பொறுத்தது. கிளவுட் கட்டமைப்பைத் தேர்ந்தெடுப்பதற்கு முன்பு நிறுவனங்கள் தங்கள் பயன்பாட்டு முறைகளை கவனமாக மதிப்பீடு செய்ய வேண்டும். பொதுவான பயன்பாடுகளுக்கு SaaS வசதியை அளிக்கும் அதே வேளையில், அதிக அளவு மற்றும் தனிப்பயன் பணிகளைக் கையாள PaaS நெகிழ்வுத்தன்மையையும் அளவிடுதலையும் வழங்குகிறது.

title: Open banking and credit risk: where lenders are finding real value
summary: Author: A finextra community member
content: Open banking is transforming how lenders approach credit risk assessment. By leveraging direct financial data, financial institutions are uncovering real value in evaluating borrower creditworthiness more accurately. This modern approach allows lenders to move beyond traditional scoring methods, offering deeper insights into customer financial behavior and improving overall lending decisions.
content_ta: Open banking மூலம் கடன் வழங்குபவர்கள் கடன் ஆபத்தை மதிப்பிடும் முறை மாறிவருகிறது. நேரடியான நிதித் தரவுகளைப் பயன்படுத்துவதன் மூலம், கடன் வாங்குபவர்களின் தகுதியை நிதி நிறுவனங்கள் மிகவும் துல்லியமாக மதிப்பிட்டு உண்மையான பலன்களைக் கண்டறிகின்றன. இந்த நவீன அணுகுமுறை பாரம்பரிய மதிப்பீட்டு முறைகளைத் தாண்டிச் செல்ல உதவுகிறது.

title: Behind the Idea: Earnix
summary:
